title: ws: option to allow a refused websocket upgrade
body:
Support a CURLWS_UPGRD_REFUSED_OK option that instructs libcurl not to error if the server refuses to upgrade a connection to Websocket.  Also reuse cached http(s) connections if available for ws(s) requests and return connections to the cache if the ws(s) connection is not upgraded.

In some circumstances a server may decide it should not or cannot upgrade to WebSocket and a client may want to know that and continue without an error.  This is allowed according to the WebSocket RFC, section 1.3 Opening Handshake: "Any status code other than 101 indicates that the WebSocket handshake has not completed and that the semantics of HTTP still apply."  I have a specific existing architecture I'd like to integrate libcurl into that requires this to work.

I understand the reasoning behind the documented behavior to fail the request if a ws(s):// scheme is requested and the server doesn't respond with a 101 switching protocol response.  However supporting this option will give the user the ability to allow it and be smarter about connection reuse.

If an upgrade is refused and the new option is set, the http(s) connection can be returned to the cache for reuse if left intact.  In addition, an http(s) connection can now be used off the cache if the url otherwise matches correctly when a WebSocket upgrade is needed.  One thing to consider might be hiding this behavior behind another option.

Full disclosure: I used AI to help me write the unit test but not any of the main library code.

@@ -64,9 +64,10 @@ directions.
 
 If the given WebSocket URL (using `ws://` or `wss://`) fails to get upgraded
 via a 101 response code and instead gets another response code back from the
-HTTP server - the transfer returns `CURLE_HTTP_RETURNED_ERROR` for that
-transfer. Note then that even 2xx response codes are then considered error
-since it failed to provide a WebSocket transfer.
+HTTP server - the transfer returns `CURLE_WS_DENIED` for that transfer. Note
+then that even 2xx response codes are then considered error. However the HTTP
+transfer is completed if the response is otherwise valid. The connection may
+be kept and returned to the cache for reuse.

@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="US-ASCII"?>
+<testcase>
+<info>
+<keywords>
+WebSockets
+</keywords>
+</info>
+
+# Server-side
+<reply>
+<data crlf="headers" nocheck="yes">
+HTTP/1.1 200 OK
+Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2010 14:49:00 GMT
+Server: test-server/fake
+Content-Length: 11
+
+no upgrade
+</data>
+</reply>
+
+# Client-side
+<client>
+# require Debug for the forced CURL_ENTROPY
+<features>
+Debug
+ws
+verbose-strings
+</features>
+<setenv>
+CURL_ENTROPY=12345678
+</setenv>
+<server>
+http
+</server>
+<tool>
+lib%TESTNUMBER
+</tool>
+<name>
+Refused WebSocket upgrade returns CURLE_WS_DENIED and connection reused
+</name>
+<command>
+- %HOSTIP %HTTPPORT
+</command>
+</client>
+
+# Verify data after the test has been "shot"
+<verify>
+<protocol crlf="headers">
+GET /path/ws/%TESTNUMBER HTTP/1.1
+Host: %HOSTIP:%HTTPPORT
+Accept: */*
+Upgrade: websocket
+Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
+Sec-WebSocket-Key: NDMyMTUzMjE2MzIxNzMyMQ==
+Connection: Upgrade
+
+GET /path/http/%TESTNUMBER HTTP/1.1
+Host: %HOSTIP:%HTTPPORT
+Accept: */*
+
+</protocol>
+<strip>
+^Host:.*
+</strip>
+### We don't want to see this:
+# * closing connection #0
+<file name="%LOGDIR/stderr%TESTNUMBER" mode="text">
+* WebSocket upgrade refused with HTTP 200
+* Connection #0 to host %HOSTIP:%HTTPPORT left intact
+* Refused WebSocket upgrade: 200
+Request 1 (WS refused) completed. CURLcode: 102 (WebSocket denied by server). HTTP Code: 200.
+* Reusing existing http: connection with host %HOSTIP
+* Connection #0 to host %HOSTIP:%HTTPPORT left intact
+Request 2 (HTTP OK) completed. HTTP Code: 200.
+</file>
+<stripfile>
+$_ = '' if(($_ !~ /left intact/) and ($_ !~ /closing connection/) and ($_ !~ /WebSocket upgrade/) and ($_ !~ /Reusing existing/) and ($_ !~ /shutting down/) and ($_ !~ /^Request \d/))
+</stripfile>
+</verify>
+</testcase>
